clue.text: Singer recollecting old times

indicators.note: recollecting read as re-collecting: the letters of the two words are gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A vocalist reminisces about the good old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollecting' looks like remembering, but read as re-collecting it rearranges OLD TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodist is a composer or performer of tunes, so a vocalist qualifies.

clue.text: Common mum having a country swim?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum, mother
someone taking a dip in the countryside would be in a stream

explanation.surface: A mother takes a dip in a rural river, as ordinary people do.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is cryptic: a mother having a country swim is MA IN STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream means conventional or normal, belonging to the common majority.

clue.text: Old comedian having no room for new stars

indicators.note: having no room for tells us a letter is taken out of the comedian's name

parts.note: Dan Leno was a Victorian music-hall comedian

explanation.surface: A veteran comic has no space left for up-and-coming celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities; it is a constellation. Dan Leno was a famous British music-hall comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is a constellation and sign of the zodiac, a group of stars.

clue.text: Imprisonment in old city interrupting trip

indicators.note: interrupting tells us the city breaks into the word for trip

parts.note: to trip the light fantastic is to dance
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone is jailed in an ancient city, cutting short their journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey; it is a dance step. Ur is the crosswords' favourite ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Durance is an old word for imprisonment, as in durance vile.

clue.text: Like an additional image? Great —- I am ready for the artist!

parts.note: super means great, excellent
I am contracts to I'm
a model who has posed is in position, ready to be painted

explanation.surface: An artist's model declares themselves splendidly ready to sit for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the surface is an artist's model eager to sit; the definition's question mark marks it as a description rather than a dictionary term.
explanation.definitionFit: A superimposed picture is one laid over another, an extra image placed on top.

clue.text: Like tie that's a swizz put round neck?

indicators.note: put round tells us the swindle word is wrapped about the cheek word

parts.note: a swizz is British slang for a swindle, a con
neck in British slang is cheek or impudence, as is lip

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a tie which merely fastens at the collar is a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' suggests the throat a tie goes round, but it means impudence, LIP; 'swizz' is British slang for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip-on tie is one that fastens with a clip rather than being knotted, so the phrase describes that kind of tie.

clue.text: Dafter gents maybe needing support

parts.note: the gents, a men's lavatory, is one kind of loo
a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: Sillier men's toilets might need propping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' is British for a men's public toilet, and LOO is the everyday British word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is informal for crazy, so loopier is a comparative meaning dafter.

clue.text: Squishy grape? No, mate — a different fruit, please!

indicators.note: squishy describes something squashed out of shape, so the letters that follow are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper rejects a squashed grape and asks the stallholder for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squishy' rearranges GRAPE NO MATE; 'a different' points to the new fruit made from the grape.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomegranate is a fruit with a tough skin and many juicy seeds.

clue.text: Nobody can provide service for monks

definitions.meaning: not a single person, not one
one of the canonical hours of prayer kept by monks, said at the ninth hour of the day

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the monastic office of the ninth hour, around 3pm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not one person, and also names the monastic office said at the ninth hour.

clue.text: Consistent physical condition of one drunkard — below par

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a sot is a habitual drunkard
ropy is British informal for poor in quality or slightly unwell

explanation.surface: A drunk is in a steady state, if somewhat under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: ROPY is British informal for poor or off-colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotropy in physics means having the same properties in every direction, a uniform condition.

clue.text: Endless money handed out by people for monument

indicators.note: Endless tells us the benefit word loses its final letter

parts.note: the dole is state benefit money handed out to the unemployed
men here simply means people

explanation.surface: Charity cash is distributed endlessly among folk raising a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the last letter from DOLE, leaving DOL; the dole is British unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolmen is a prehistoric stone tomb, a megalithic monument of upright stones and a capstone.

clue.text: Position after chess player has taken piece is a matter for debate

indicators.note: has taken tells us the chess player is followed by the piece he took
after tells us the position word comes after the chess player and piece

parts.note: Mikhail Tal was a world chess champion
the king is a chess piece
a point is a position or place

explanation.surface: A chess master captures a piece, then the move becomes a matter of dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Mikhail Tal was world chess champion in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking point is a topic that invites discussion, a subject of debate.

clue.text: Parliamentary process that derives from the New Testament?

definitions.meaning: the stage at which a bill's general principles are debated in Parliament

definitions.text: that derives from the New Testament?
definitions.meaning: in a church service the later lesson read is often taken from the New Testament, the second part of the Bible

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is playful: the New Testament is the second part of the Bible, and in church the second lesson read often comes from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill passes through a debate stage in Parliament known by this name, and church lessons supply the second meaning.

clue.text: Composer and writer in domestic row

indicators.note: in tells us the writer goes inside the other two words

parts.note: a char is a British cleaning woman, a domestic help
a tier is a row, as of seats
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: A composer and an author are caught up in a household quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic row' suggests a family quarrel; it is CHAR (a British cleaning lady) plus TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc-Antoine Charpentier was a French Baroque composer, known for his Te Deum.

clue.text: Form of communication to engage the pupils

definitions.text: Form of communication to engage the pupils

parts.words: Form of communication to engage the pupils
parts.note: sounds like a teacher holding a class's attention, but the pupils are those of the eyes, met by a direct look

explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' suggests schoolchildren; they are the dark centres of the eyes, which a direct look engages.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting someone's gaze directly is a non-verbal means of communication that connects the pupils of two people.

clue.text: Author one of his followers fails to finish?

indicators.note: fails to finish tells us the word for a follower loses its final letter

parts.note: anyone who follows an author's books is one of his readers

explanation.surface: A writer wonders whether one of his fans will give up before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' cuts the last letter from READER; Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.

clue.text: Printer's process to produce bank-notes?

parts.note: to make something is to produce it
the ready is slang for cash, banknotes

explanation.surface: A printing technique that turns out paper money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ready' (or 'readies') is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-ready is a printing term for preparing a press and forme so impressions come out even.

clue.text: High-range instrument

parts.note: not an instrument with a high pitch, but one played high in a mountain range, in the Alps

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-range' suggests a high pitch; it means a mountain range, the Alps, where this long wooden horn is played.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpenhorn is a long wooden horn played by herdsmen in the Alps, a mountain range.

clue.text: Aeronautical engineer's housing? A small room in Geordieland

indicators.note: in tells us the room goes inside the region

parts.note: Geordies come from Tyneside in North East England, NE
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A tiny flat is offered in Newcastle, perhaps to an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Tyneside, in the North East of England, abbreviated NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined casing on an aircraft that houses an engine.

clue.text: Mark said to be "old money"

indicators.note: said to be tells us the word for mark is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to frank a letter is to mark it to show postage is paid

explanation.surface: Someone claims a mark is merely old money, as the Deutschmark became.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a currency or a name; it is the verb, to frank a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and Belgium before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Decorative church item in the van?

definitions.meaning: an ornamental cloth hung over the front of an altar
in the van means in the vanguard, at the front

explanation.walkthrough: 'van' suggests a vehicle; it is short for vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontal is an altar hanging, and the adjective means at the front, where the vanguard is.

clue.text: Biochemical substance could make one corpulent, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or inventive, so the letters before it are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a certain chemical could fatten them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like the verb 'I imagine'; it rearranges ONE CORPULENT I.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleoprotein is a compound of a protein and a nucleic acid, a biochemical substance found in cells.

clue.text: Make angry sounds at bishop making mistake

parts.note: to boo someone is to jeer at them
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers a bishop for his blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal for a silly blunder, an error.

clue.text: Old duck in anger gets another bird

indicators.note: in tells us the duck goes inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: An elderly duck gets cross and turns into a different bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the cricket score of zero, O, not the bird; 'another bird' is a nod to that false duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriole is a brightly coloured songbird, here a bird other than the misleading duck.

clue.text: Coach may only go so far to make one a winner initially

indicators.note: initially tells us the winner word comes first, before the other pieces

parts.note: a victor is a winner
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A trainer can only take a player so far towards becoming a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' seems to be a trainer; it is a horse-drawn carriage. 'may only go so far' is a nod to London's Victoria Coach Station, where coaches terminate.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a type of coach.

clue.text: Inlet that's upset by slight wind

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the wind word reads bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a light breeze

explanation.surface: A creek is disturbed by a gentle breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a long narrow sea inlet formed by a drowned river valley.

clue.text: Composer who performs on the fringe?

definitions.meaning: Samuel ... was the American composer of the Adagio for Strings
one who works on a fringe of hair, cutting it

explanation.walkthrough: 'performs on the fringe' suggests a fringe theatre performer; the fringe is a cut of hair at the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Barber was an American composer, and a hairdresser for men trims fringes.

clue.text: Endless stand against fighting by pacifist ultimately dependable

indicators.note: Endless tells us the word for a stand loses its final letter

parts.note: a stall is a stand at a market
war means fighting

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of pacifist

explanation.surface: An unreliable stance against war is finally made trustworthy by a pacifist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the final letter of the stand word; 'against' and 'by' are only placing words, setting the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stalwart is loyal and reliable, so dependable is a synonym.
